name: Food truck park
summary: Cost is driven by fixed shared amenities (restroom building, shade pavilion, seating plaza, lighting, grease handling) spread over a small number of truck pads, so cost per pad falls steeply with pad count. Public data are thin: a few municipal budgets/bids (Moses Lake WA, Albert Lea MN, Tyrone GA, North Summit UT) and Texas TDLR project registrations give a wide $30k–$200k+/pad spread; the mid is a reasoned build-up and should be verified.

typicalSize.method: Public examples range from 3 pads (Albert Lea e2, Universal City e9) through 6 (Moses Lake e1) to 6–9 (San Antonio e4); purpose-built private parks commonly run 8–20. Mid of 10 is a judgment for a stand-alone commercial park.

primaryUnitsPerAcre.method: Each truck pad ~12x40 ft (~500 SF, cf. 425 SF pad in e5) plus service drive, seating plaza, restroom/shade and ~4–6 parking spaces per pad. ~2,500–5,000 SF of site per pad gives ~9–17 pads/acre; rounded.

parkingPerPrimaryUnit.method: Universal City TX 2026 agenda (e10) planned 3 trucks with 10 parking spaces (~3.3/pad). Suburban stand-alone parks typically need more; mid 5 spaces per pad is a judgment, local zoning governs.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Sourced anchors: minimal court (pad + power, no restrooms) Albert Lea e2 = $92,693/3 pads = ~$31k/pad (2023); full-amenity 6-truck plaza Moses Lake e1 low bid $598k/6 = ~$100k/pad, high bid ~$200k/pad (2023); San Antonio e4 $2.7M for 6–9 trucks (~$300k–$450k/pad, multi-story structure, treated as outlier above high). Cross-check build-up for 10 pads: pad + pedestal + trenching ~$25k/pad (e5: 425 SF pad $8k + $10k electrical) = $250k; restroom building ~$200k (e7 $180k, e8 $250k); shade pavilion ~$250k (e6); paving/parking/lighting/landscape ~$250k; grease handling ~$40k; total ~$1.0M = ~$100k/pad. Mid $90k sits between the Moses Lake low bid and the build-up, slightly discounted for national (Moses Lake is WA). Low = minimal court with off-site restrooms (e2, e3); high = Moses Lake upper bid level.

scope.notes: Per pad, includes pro-rata share of shared amenities (restroom building, shade, seating plaza hardscape, lighting, on-site utilities, parking). Contractor price incl. GC and OH&P; excludes land, soft costs, loose furniture, off-site utility extensions, impact/tap fees.

qualityTiers.method: Economy = low/mid (35k/90k ≈ 0.4, rounded up); premium = high/mid (200/90 ≈ 2.2) treated as luxury; premium interpolated. The wide spread reflects whether restrooms, shade and a bar building are included.

systemSplit.method: Derived from the 10-pad build-up in hardCost.method: site paving/hardscape/landscape (32) and site utilities/pedestal feeders (33) dominate; electrical (26) covers pedestals, lighting and service; restroom building split across 03/06/07/08/09/10/22; shade structure in 05/13. General conditions ~15% in e5 bid, reduced to 10% here because GC fee is partly in trades' OH&P.

lineItems.name: Truck pad (concrete, ~450 SF) with utility pedestal (power, water) and trenching

cost.method: e5 (UT, 2023): 425 SF pad at $18.86/SF = $8,016 plus $10,000 LS electrical for the truck = ~$18k before 15% GC; ~$21k with GC. Mid rounded to $22k; high adds water/sewer stub and 50A+ service with longer runs; low = power-only pedestal with gravel pad.

lineItems.notes: Carve-out of the baseline; shown for reference.

lineItems.name: Restroom building (site-built or prefab, ~400–600 SF)

cost.method: e7 Edinburg TX: $180,000 for 510 SF restroom building + restriping (2025); e8 Brownsville TX: $250,000 for 559 SF restrooms/storage plus slabs, sidewalks and parking (2024). Mid ~$190k; low for a small prefab unit; high for larger/full-finish buildings outside Texas.

lineItems.notes: Included in baseline at typical size; parks that use adjacent public restrooms (e3) can omit it.

cost.method: e6 Walsh (Fort Worth TX, 2022): $250,000 / 6,100 SF ≈ $41/SF for a fully covered shade structure with concrete/DG seating area, furniture and planting. Low = fabric shade sails; high = steel-framed metal-roof pavilion. Per SF of covered area.

lineItems.name: Shared grease interceptor / grease disposal station (~1,000 gal)

cost.method: No reliable public bid found. Forum anecdotes put a 1,000-gal tank at $5–8k plus $10–20k install (not cited as evidence, low quality). Mid assumes precast in-ground unit with excavation, traffic lid and connections; high where sewer drops to each pad and a larger unit are required. Verify against local utility requirements.

lineItems.notes: Only needed where trucks discharge grey/grease water on site; many parks require trucks to self-contain.

lineItems.name: Shared commissary kitchen / cold storage

cost.method: Derived: small commercial kitchen building cost ($/SF) by analogy to restaurant/QSR shell plus kitchen fit-out; not sourced specifically. Applies to parks that offer commissary services (e.g., e4 includes a commissary and cold storage).

lineItems.notes: Optional; some jurisdictions require trucks to operate from a licensed commissary.

cost.method: Derived: 600–1,200 SF bar building with walk-in and bar equipment at ~$250–500/SF. Not sourced; common revenue anchor for private parks.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Picnic tables, umbrellas, trash/recycling receptacles, string lights and games: ~4–8 tables per pad at $500–1,200 each. Derived.

pctOfHard.method: Site-centric project with simple buildings: civil/site design, small-building architecture, permits, survey/geotech, testing. Lower than buildings (~20–25%) because architecture scope is small. Derived; Tyrone GA used design-build (e3), which compresses separate design fees.

softCosts.notes: Add health-department plan review, food-truck park zoning/SUP and utility capacity studies where required.

design.method: Small public projects have run well over early estimates: Moses Lake bids were 18%–140% over the $505k earmark (e1). Use a higher-than-normal design contingency at concept stage.

hard.method: Sitework-heavy scope with utility unknowns; typical 5–10% construction contingency.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Min ≈ Albert Lea minimal court (e2, ~$31k/pad); max ≈ Moses Lake high bid ($200k/pad, e1) plus soft costs and allowance; e4 (~$300k+/pad, multi-story) sits at the top edge.

source.title: Moses Lake Scraps Food Truck Park Project Amid Rising Costs, City Manager Confirms

evidence.quote: space for six food trucks, seating, shade structures, and restroom facilities. The city had earmarked around $505,000 ... proposals ranging from approximately $598,000 to over $1.2 million.
evidence.scopeNotes: Bid prices (hard cost) for a 6-truck municipal plaza with restrooms and shade; bids rejected in 2023. $100k–$200k per pad.

source.title: Albert Lea City Council gives green light for food truck court

evidence.quote: The City Council accepted the bid of $92,693 to create the food truck court. ... landscaping, power hook-ups and a concrete pad for up to three food trucks.
evidence.scopeNotes: Minimal court: no restrooms or shade; city parks crews supplied most landscaping and benches. ~$31k per pad. Published 2023-03-03.

evidence.quote: The budget for this project has been established not to exceed $150,000.
evidence.scopeNotes: Design-build NTE budget; compacted aggregate (no paving) for trucks, restrooms are next door (not built), single hose bib, stage alternate. Pad count not stated.

source.title: Brothers plan to open $2.7M food truck park east of downtown by Fiesta

evidence.quote: The project started out as a $500,000 project, and four years later, it's nearly a $2.7 million project. ... space for about six to nine food trucks
evidence.scopeNotes: Total project cost (likely incl. soft costs) for a three-story open-air structure with commissary and cold storage; outlier, used only to bound the high end.

source.title: Universal City looks to approve development agreement for food truck park

evidence.quote: The food truck park will have space for three food trucks along with 10 parking spaces.
evidence.scopeNotes: Program only, no cost. 10/3 = 3.3 spaces per pad.

openQuestions: Need 2–3 more completed (not bid/estimate) private food truck park budgets with pad counts, especially 8–20 pad parks.
Grease interceptor and per-pad sewer requirements vary by utility; a sourced installed cost is still missing.
Parking ratio per pad is assumed; check zoning codes in target markets.
